title: Infografía de Hoja de Ruta de Cuatro Etapas del Viaje de Machine Learning
prompt:
Multidimensional Impacts of Global Warming on Ecosystems

Overall style and composition: Create a complex, professional, futuristic data visualization infographic with a dark data flow grid background. The overall color scheme adopts a "climate crisis" palette: center features fiery orange-red contrasting with deep blue, gradually transitioning outward to warning yellow and data-representing cool gray/purple. Title at top in prominent uppercase letters: "GLOBAL WARMING: ECOSYSTEM IMPACTS & ACCELERATION (1900-2025 DATA VISUALIZATION)".

1. Central Core: Feverish Earth
Image center features a semi-transparent, glowing Earth hologram. Earth surface shows not just land and ocean, but covered with pulsating red light representing heat, especially in Arctic and equatorial regions. A subtle glowing thermometer icon inserted into Earth core, reading displays "CURRENT STATUS: +1.15°C WARMING (Relative to Pre-industrial)".

2. Three Major Trend Curves Surrounding Core (Past Century 1900-2025)
Surrounding central Earth are three prominent, data-marked dynamic curve graphs orbiting like trajectories. Each curve has clear starting point (1900) and endpoint (2025), with key thresholds marked.

Curve A (Top, Fiery Red): Global Temperature Anomaly
- Curve shape: Initially slow rise, sharply steep increase after 1980
- Key data points: 1900: "-0.1°C baseline", 1980: "+0.25°C", 2025: "+1.15°C (Highest on record)"
- Annotation: Small icon showing "Paris Agreement 1.5°C warning line" approaching

Curve B (Middle, Deep Blue): Sea Level Rise
- Curve shape: Continuous, accelerating upward curve
- Key data points: 1900: "0 mm reference", 1993: "+100mm", 2025: "+230mm (Accelerating Rate: >4mm/yr)"
- Annotation: Below in small text "Thermal Expansion & Ice Melt Contribution"

Curve C (Bottom, Purple-gray with smoke effect): Atmospheric CO₂ Concentration
- Curve shape: Steepest exponential growth curve, breaking historical safe limits
- Key data points: 1900: "~295 ppm", 1950: "315 ppm", 1988: "350 ppm (Safe Limit Breached)", 2025: ">423 ppm (Unprecedented in 2M years)"

3. Left Panel: Extreme Events & Biodiversity Crisis (Visual Evidence)
Upper block: Intensified Extreme Weather - Three circular miniature satellite view windows showing heatwaves/wildfires, hurricanes, and extreme rainfall/floods with data labels.

Lower block: Accelerating Biodiversity Loss - Funnel-shaped chart showing species extinction rate 100x-1000x higher than background rate, with key data: "1 MILLION SPECIES AT RISK (IPBES Report)", ">90% Coral Reefs at risk at 1.5°C warming"

4. Right Panel: Key Resource Pressures (Schematic Impacts)
Upper block: Agriculture & Food Security Strain - Split world map showing drought-cracked land and melting permafrost, projected yield decline up to -20% for major crops

Lower block: Water Scarcity & Glacial Retreat - Retreating mountain glacier feeding drying river, low reservoir showing cracked bottom, "2+ Billion People living in high water stress regions"

8K resolution, professional data visualization, futuristic aesthetic.
